neighbours.label: A verb or noun naming a hostile clash or collision event (ran into trouble, fought a war, crashed into, were beaten back), vs the same frames describing a neutral or cooperative event
fire: Halfway through the launch we ran into serious problems with the servers.
The two clans fought a long and bloody war over the valley.
On the icy road his car skidded and slammed into a parked van.
The rebels charged the fort but were driven back by heavy fire.
Within a week the new manager clashed with the entire board.
The cyclist lost control on the descent and crashed into a barrier.
During the strike, protesters fought with police outside the factory.
The expedition soon ran into a blizzard that trapped them for days.

The two clans shared a long and peaceful border along the valley.
On the quiet road his car rolled slowly into a parking space.
The visitors toured the fort and were shown around by a guide.
Within a week the new manager met with the entire board.
The cyclist slowed down on the descent and waved at a neighbor.
During the holiday, families picnicked on the lawn outside the factory.
The expedition soon reached a village that hosted them for days.
